claims.claim: Hesychius of Jerusalem was a Christian priest (presbyter) of Jerusalem.
Hesychius of Jerusalem was active during the first half of the fifth century, with approximate dates of birth and death uncertain (possibly died c. 450 or in the 450s).
Hesychius served as a priest in the church in Jerusalem around 412 and was recognized by 429 as the pre-eminent biblical interpreter and teacher of the church in Jerusalem and Palestine.
The work In sanctum Andream (Homily 7) is an encomium (eulogy) on the Apostle Andrew the First-Called.
The homily was preached during the saint's celebration at the church of the Anastasis in Jerusalem on 30 November.
The work was written in Greek at Jerusalem in the early 5th century.
The homily is listed as Sermon 7 in Migne's edition (Patrologia Graeca 93).
The work survives in manuscript tradition and is catalogued as CPG 6571 and BHG 104.
The homily was read and summarized by Photius in his Bibliotheca (codex 269).
Hesychius was renowned for his allegorical and mystical interpretations of Scripture and was acclaimed as having annotated the whole of sacred Scripture.
The authenticity of some works attributed to Hesychius is debated because there were many writers with the name Hesychius and their works are often mixed.
Hesychius played a prominent role in the 5th-century controversy on the nature of Christ and wrote a church history after 428 that controverted Nestorianism.
